_what: The real AgentDojo attack corpus, generated by the real installed agentdojo package. Every string here is what agentdojo's own BaseAttack.attack() returned for one (attack, user task, injection task) triple, deduplicated per attack.
_how_generated: pip install <clone> into an isolated venv (the package pulls openai/anthropic/cohere/langchain/google-genai and was deliberately NOT installed into this project's interpreter), then the script under _generator_source was run against it. It imports agentdojo.attacks so every @register_attack class registers, walks ATTACKS, instantiates each with the four real v1 suites (workspace, travel, banking, slack) and a stub pipeline named 'gpt-4o-2024-05-13' (a real key of agentdojo.models.MODEL_NAMES, so their own get_model_name_from_pipeline resolves to 'GPT-4'), and calls the real attack() for every user-task x injection-task pair. attack() runs their real GroundTruthPipeline to find the injection slots -- no LLM is involved anywhere in this, and none was called.
_exclusions: 'manual' is the 17th registered attack and is excluded: it has no template, it calls input() to ask a human for the injection string (attacks/baseline_attacks.py:18-27). DoS attacks ignore the {goal} placeholder, so each contributes exactly one distinct string.
_known_defect_in_the_reference: TaskSuite.check() returns False for every user task in all four v1 suites in this environment, so generate_injections() -- which gates on it -- raises. attack() itself works and is what was called. The gate is about ground-truth replay of the *user* tasks and has no bearing on the attack strings, which come from a fixed template formatted with the injection task's own GOAL.
